ch1_open.notes: GDD Ch1: Commander Veyra assigns the Emberfall mission; senior recruiter Dagen accompanies. Dagen never speaks. This node establishes the Litany of Hollowing and Veyra's standing.
text: Greyhold's hall is cold enough to see your breath. Commander Veyra sets a folded report on the table between you and does not open it.
Emberfall stopped sending word three days ago. Dagen stands at the door with his mouth shut, as he has for three years. The Litany is still sung at dusk.

ch1_road.notes: Travel beat. Sets the three days of quiet and the feeling that something upstream is wrong.
text: The road to Emberfall runs downhill through wet ash. Three days, and Dagen has not said one word that was not necessary.
No smoke. No bodies. No Hollowed in the fields, which is the part that should comfort you and does not.

ch1_bridge.notes: CLASS GATE 1 of 3 in Act 1. The collapsed bridge. Each class has its own solution; two of three choices are disabled for any given run. The disabled ones stay visible on purpose.
text: The creek has taken the bridge apart. Half of it lies in the water, and the rest holds the far bank up by stubbornness.
Only one way across, and it depends on what you are. Dagen watches to see which way you reach for it.

choices.label: Smash the beams into a ramp

ch1_bridge_warrior.notes: Warrior route. Loud, slow, and it announces you to anything listening.
text: You put your shoulder under the beam and lift until the water runs brown. What was a wall becomes a ramp, and a ramp becomes a road.
It costs you. Everything on this road is going to cost you something, and the Hollowing does not accept receipts.

ch1_bridge_archer.notes: Archer route. Quiet, and it costs time — the ford is longer.
text: The cart ruts go right where the water looks deepest, which is where the old ford ran before the bank gave. You follow them and keep dry.
Dagen says nothing, but he stops at the water edge to watch you find it, and that is as close as he comes to praise.

ch1_bridge_mage.notes: Mage route. The runes still hold. Releasing them properly is quiet and precise.
text: The stones are still standing because of the runes on them, not in spite of them. You read the sealing, and the sealing lets you pass.
Aether is cheaper than strength and dearer than either. You pay the small price and step over the creek on nothing at all.

ch1_regroup.notes: Camp before the village. A rest node: pays restExp from balance.json and tops the class pool.
text: You make camp a half mile short of Emberfall, where the palisade is still a shape against the dark.
No lanterns in the village. No dogs. Whatever happened here happened inside, and it happened fast.

ch1_gates.notes: CLASS GATE 2 of 3. The village gates are locked from the inside. Nothing in Emberfall has opened them in days.
text: Emberfall's gates are shut, and the bolt is on the inside. Somebody did that on purpose, with their own hands, a long time ago.
You could go over. Dagen would not stop you. But a village that locked itself away has a reason, and the reason is in the hall.

ch1_gates_warrior.notes: Warrior route. The village hears you arrive. That is a cost, not a free move.
text: The gate comes off its hinges with a sound like a dropped cart. You walk in through the hole you made, and the dark on the other side does not move.
Dagen enters behind you and says, at last, one word. It is not a compliment. It is the word people use for a door.

ch1_gates_archer.notes: Archer route. Quiet entry over the wall. You see the village before it sees you.
text: The villagers never used the gate. A yard wall at the back is low, mossy, and worn smooth in the middle where a hundred shoulders went.
You come down it quiet and stop with a hand up. Ahead, a light under a door, and someone breathing too fast.

ch1_gates_mage.notes: Mage route. The lock opens cleanly. Nobody hears it, which is its own kind of problem.
text: The lock answers to aether as a knot answers to a finger. You open it without touching the iron, and the gate swings like it was never barred.
A whisper of aether carries you over the threshold, and the air inside tastes of old smoke and older fear.

ch1_village.notes: Inside Emberfall. The village is intact and nobody is working. Nobody is outside at all.
text: Emberfall is a village holding its breath. Doors barred, ash in the hearths, every shutter closed against a dark that came from under the ground.
One light is still burning, in the hall, where the meeting house would be. Whoever is in there has been waiting for a knock.

ch1_senna.notes: Mother Senna. The GDD's only named civilian in Act 1's opening. She has been hiding since the third day of silence.
text: Mother Senna is on the floor by the hearth with a poker held like a knife. She has the look of someone who has been alone long enough to talk to furniture.
The reports stopped because Elder Oswin told them to stop. She has heard chanting under the floor since Michaelmas, and it has a word in it: her granddaughter's name.

ch1_descent.notes: Senna leads you to the cellar stairs under the village hall. The air changes here.
text: Under the hall there are stairs nobody put on the village plan. The air comes up them warm, and it carries a sound that is almost, but not quite, singing.
Dagen stops at the top. He has gone grey. Whatever is down there, he has heard it before.

ch1_oswin.notes: Elder Oswin, half-turned into a Choir Vessel, and connected to Elin. This node must not resolve anything — it sets up the dilemma.
text: Elder Oswin is on his knees in a circle cut into the floor, and the change in him has gone most of the way. His mouth keeps moving on a word that is not his.
From his chest, threads of dark run out to the centre of the rune, and from the centre to a girl asleep in the middle of it. Pale. Breathing. Thirteen, at a guess.

choices.label: Face what is in the cellar

ch1_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 1 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED outcome is Option B: the Vigil's emergency binding ritual. Option A is undefined in the GDD and must be written without contradicting later acts. Both branches must converge on ch1_elin, where Elin's fate is decided — that keeps the structure shared while the prose diverges.
text: It is not a monster. That is the part you cannot put down. It is a man on his knees with something growing in him, and the threads go both ways.
Cut the seed and the singing stops here, and so does Oswin. Keep him bound and something in him keeps growing, slowly, where nobody is counting.

ch1_outcome_destroy.notes: Option A. Undefined in the GDD. Reward shape should mirror Option B's per the reward table: main-branch choices move a big reputation swing plus small courage. Villager survival differs by design.
text: You end it, and it ends quickly, like a held breath let out. The threads go out of Elin and the girl comes up out of the circle shaking and alive.
Oswin does not come up at all. Dagen will not meet your eye, and the villagers are grateful in the way of people who are afraid of what you might do next.

ch1_outcome_rescue.notes: Option B — DETERMINED by the GDD. The Vigil's emergency binding ritual works: Oswin survives but is weakened, Elin is safe, the villagers are grateful, and a small seed of Hollowing survives in Oswin. This node also flags the continuation so later chapters can check it.
text: The Vigil's binding ritual is four words and a knife held wrong on purpose. You say them. The threads go slack, and Oswin breathes like a man again.
He lives. He is not all there, and everyone in the cellar can see the part that is not. But Elin is safe, and the hall is full of people saying so.

ch1_elin.notes: Elin, the person Oswin was connected to. In the DETERMINED branch Elin is safe. Under Option A the GDD does not say, and this node is where you decide what happens to her.
text: Elin wakes with no memory of the circle and a burn on her palm in the shape of the rune. She asks where her grandfather is. You tell her he is alive.
It is true, and it is not the whole of it, and she is thirteen, and there is no version of tonight that lets you say it all.

choices.label: Carry it back to the surface

ch1_aftermath.notes: The village is grateful, and the incident is not an accident: the Choir is operating somewhere with access. Closes the chapter's evidence beat.
text: By morning the villagers have decided you are the reason Emberfall is still a village. They are warm about it, and loud, and nobody mentions the cellar.
Dagen finally speaks a whole sentence. It is: this was not random, and we have been sent here before.

ch1_litany.notes: Chapter close. The Litany mentions the Shepherd arriving when 'the fields are ready for harvest'. This is the hook into Chapter 2's Harrow's Reach objective.
text: The Litany was under Senna's floor, in her hand, in a language she cannot read. It names a place, Harrow's Reach. It names a season.
And then the line you will not forget, sung over and over, patient as a harvest: the fields are ready.

ch1_ending.notes: Formerly the slice ending. With Chapters 2-8 written, this is the road home and the rest beat before Chapter 2; the real Act 1 ending is ch8_watchtower_meet.
text: Emberfall keeps its gates open that night, for the first time in three days, and Dagen walks out through them without looking back at the hall.
The road home is uneventful, which is its own kind of news. You sleep in shifts, and the seed of Hollowing you left breathing in an old man keeps its own counsel.

ch2_open.notes: GDD Ch2: Greyhold, healing hall and council chamber. Three nights after Emberfall. Oswin talks in delirium; candles die at midnight. The seed inside him is a fragment of consciousness trying to speak.
text: Greyhold's healing hall smells of wax and ash. Oswin has been given a cot by the wall, and every night at midnight the candles nearest him go out.
Not blown. Not burned down. Out. Three nights running, and tonight you are awake to see it, and so is Veyra.

ch2_delirium.notes: GDD Ch2: Veyra questions the team's Emberfall decision but stands by them. This node must not resolve anything - it sets up the Whisper.
text: Veyra does not dress it up. Bringing Oswin back was a choice, and the choices you carry come home to roost in her hall, not yours.
Then she says the part that matters: you made the call a Vigil soldier is supposed to make, and she will stand in front of the council and say so.

ch2_whisper.notes: GDD Ch2: Oswin's shadow detaches into a Whisper, a smoky entity trying to convey a message. A real fight: it has to be put down before the words in it can be trusted. Drop is act1_whisper_ash.
text: Midnight comes. The candles die in a row, and Oswin's shadow stands up off the floor without him.
It is smoke given a suggestion of bones, and it has his voice, or the Hollowing's idea of his voice. It wants to say something. Everything in the room wants you to let it.

ch2_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery. The Vigil does not leave its soldiers where they fall. A little EXP so losing is never a dead stop, and the story keeps its shape.
text: The Whisper leans over you like weather. Then boots, and steel, and the healer's grey light - the hall watch heard the candles go out and came ready.
You wake on the cold flagstones with Dagen's hand around your arm and the shadow burned down to a stain. It said nothing after all. You are going to have to earn the message instead.

ch2_message.notes: GDD Ch2: with the Whisper put down, the words come loose - the fields... Harrow's Reach... the harvest comes.
text: The ash where it stood holds a shape for a moment, and the shape holds words, the way a bell holds a note after the strike.
...the fields... Harrow's Reach... the harvest comes... Then nothing, and Oswin sleeps without the candles caring.

ch2_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 2 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED outcome is Option A: destroy the Whisper completely. Oswin is secured, the seed is destroyed, and the team keeps only the name Harrow's Reach - no details on timing, which is the point: urgency without a deadline. Both branches converge on ch2_council.
text: The healers can burn the stain out of the stones tonight. Oswin sleeps through it, and wakes cleared of it, or mostly - and the message dies with the last of the smoke.
Or you keep what it was trying to say, sealed in a warded jar, and every week it sits there is a week something in it sits there too.

ch2_outcome_destroy.notes: GDD DETERMINED branch: Option A. Oswin fully secured; the team keeps one location name and nothing else. Flag set so later chapters can reference the clean choice.
text: The healers light the pyre-pan and the stain fights it for the length of one held breath. Then it is ash, and Oswin is only an old man, weeping at nothing.
You are left with a name - Harrow's Reach - and no idea when the harvest is. The not-knowing is the weapon. Somebody built it that way on purpose.

choices.label: Take the name to the council

ch2_outcome_preserve.notes: Non-determined branch, written to not contradict later acts: the fragment is warded but the GDD's outcome facts (name kept, no timing) still hold, because the warded jar keeps the words without yielding more. Flag set to the same key only if the seed is secured - here it is contained, not destroyed, so a separate flag.
text: The jar takes the stain as a riverbed takes a river. The Arcanum mages warded it in three languages, and one of them did not meet your eye afterwards.
Oswin is cleared of it either way. What is in the jar still says the fields, still says the harvest, and still says nothing about when.

choices.label: Take the name to the council

ch2_council.notes: Chapter close. Harrow's Reach becomes the next objective without a deadline. Hooks into Ch3's wheat-farming region on the Iron Concordat border.
text: The council chamber is warmer than the hall and twice as cold. Harrow's Reach is wheat country, Iron Concordat soil, a day's ride past the last Vigil patrol.
Veyra gives you the road because there is nobody else to give it to. Harvests do not wait for councils to finish arguing.

ch3_open.notes: GDD Ch3: Harrow's Reach, a wheat-farming region on the Iron Concordat border. The village carries a wrong calmness. Objective: learn what the Choir is planning before the harvest, with no idea how much time remains.
text: Harrow's Reach is golden in a way that has nothing to do with health. The wheat is taller than a rider and the lanes are swept, and nothing anywhere is afraid.
Dagen stops at the boundary stone and will not go past it. You are beginning to understand that his silences are a map, and this one says here.

ch3_fields.notes: GDD Ch3: the wheat fields form a massive sigil only visible from high ground. From the lane it is just farming.
text: From the lane the fields are furrows. From the mill mound they are something else: a pattern cut in the wheat, wide as the village, centred on the barn.
It is not a symbol you know. It is the shape of one, the way a mask is the shape of a face.

ch3_callen.notes: GDD Ch3: Reeve Callen enthusiastically invites the team to the evening's Harvest Festival - clearly under a mass pacification spell.
text: Reeve Callen meets you at his own gate with both hands out and a smile that never once reaches up. You are expected, he says. Everyone is expected.
The Harvest Festival is tonight. There has never been less to celebrate in a place so certain there has never been more.

ch3_watch.notes: GDD Ch3: the militia stands guard without genuine alertness. The village watches back without watching.
text: The militia at the barn hold spears like props and look through you at nothing. They are guarding something, and none of them know what.
Dagen finally speaks. He says the word the whole village is circling without saying: harvest. Then he checks his blade, once, the way other men pray.

ch3_midnight.notes: GDD Ch3: at midnight the entire village gathers around the barn, chanting unconsciously. Callen's body begins sprouting the Shepherd's Emissary. Sets up the class gate on breaking the sigil.
text: Midnight, and the village walks in its sleep. Every door opens at once, and the chant comes up out of the ground rather than out of the people drifting to the barn.
Callen stands in the middle of them, and something is starting to use his body the way a hand uses a glove. Kill the sigil's feed, or fight what it becomes.

ch3_gates.notes: CLASS GATE 3 of 3 in Act 1. Disrupting the sigil is class-specific: Warrior shatters the anchor stone, Archer severs the rune-line from the loft, Mage rewrites the pattern from inside. The GDD's DETERMINED outcome is Option B - break the spell before fighting.
text: The pattern holds because something in it anchors. At the barn's corner a waist-high stone drinks the moonlight and gives none of it back, and a rune-line runs from it up into the loft beams.
Whatever you do to that pattern, you do in front of the whole chanting village.

ch3_gates_warrior.notes: Warrior route. Loud, direct, and it wakes the Emissary early.
text: You put your blade through the anchor stone the way a woodcutter takes a knot out of a plank. It takes four blows, and on the fourth the wheat goes flat in a ring a mile wide.
The chant stops mid-word. Every sleeping face in the crowd frowns, as a sleeper frowns when a floorboard creaks.

ch3_gates_archer.notes: Archer route. One shot, from the loft, while the village sleeps standing up.
text: You go up the outside of the loft on the stack pallets and put one arrow through the rune-line where it crosses the beam, at the knot where the pattern is thinnest.
The line parts like a cut harp string. The note under the world loses its pitch, and the wheat lies down as if a hand had smoothed it.

ch3_gates_mage.notes: Mage route. Not destruction - authorship. The pattern is written, so it can be re-written.
text: You step into the pattern instead of breaking it, and read it as the Ashwarden records read: as an instruction. Then you give it a different one.
A sigil this old expects obedience. It gets grammar instead. The wheat folds along new lines, and the chant comes apart into ordinary breathing.

ch3_sigil.notes: GDD Ch3 DETERMINED outcome in progress: the spell is broken first, so the villagers will survive whatever comes. The Emissary rises from Callen. Flag ch3_spell_broken records the safe-village branch.
text: The village wakes as one sleeper wakes - confusion, then noise. And out of that noise Callen's body stands up wrong, unfolding into something built to carry a message.
It wears his outline the way the mask wore the face. Behind you, people scream, run, live. Whatever it does next, it does to you.

ch3_evac.notes: Reinforces the GDD's outcome: villagers survive unharmed. Costs time - the Emissary gathers itself - which is paid for in the fight, not in blood.
text: You put yourself between it and the crowd and roar the Vigil's retreat-call until the field drains of villagers. It costs you a hundred heartbeats you will want back.
The Emissary uses every one of them. By the time the last child is over the fence, it has finished deciding what it is.

ch3_fight.notes: GDD Ch3: the Shepherd's Emissary - a partial form of the Sable Shepherd, manifested through a vessel. Because the spell was broken first (DETERMINED Option B), the fight is harder but the village lives. Drop is act1_emissary_seal.
text: The Shepherd's Emissary comes off the barn wall like a shadow learning to walk. It does not hurry. It has never once needed to hurry.
Behind it, the village is awake and screaming, and in front of it there is only you.

ch3_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery. Because the spell was broken first (flag ch3_spell_broken), the village survives even when the player goes down - the DETERMINED outcome holds either way.
text: The Emissary puts you into the wheat like a threshing arm. But the pattern is broken and the vessel is empty of its congregation, and a thing built to be fed starves in the open.
The outriders find you at dawn. The Emissary is a stain and a smell. Callen sits on his doorstep, asking what day it is.

choices.label: Stand up and count the cost

ch3_after.notes: GDD Ch3 outcome: all villagers survive unharmed and Callen recovers fully. He begins recalling fragments - which become Ch4's testimony.
text: By noon Callen is Callen again, hollow-eyed and sick with what his hands nearly did. The village counts itself and comes out even: every soul, not one lost.
He keeps starting sentences and stopping. Something is trying to surface in him, and it is not a chant this time. It is memory.

ch4_open.notes: GDD Ch4: bring Callen to testify before the Council; convince them the threat is real and spreading.
text: Callen rides to Greyhold between Vigil soldiers, wrapped in a borrowed cloak, talking the whole way - to himself, to the road, to nobody.
He does not remember doing any of it. He remembers wanting, very badly, to be part of something. The Choir does not recruit with knives. It recruits with belonging.

ch4_council.notes: GDD Ch4: during the hearing, suspicion falls on Magus Thessaly, the Arcanum Tower representative, who grows fidgety whenever the Hollowing is raised.
text: The three-faction council sits under Greyhold's oldest roof. Emberfall is disputed. Harrow's Reach is disputed. The Litany is produced, translated, and argued over line by line.
Only one person in the room does not look at the Litany at all. Magus Thessaly, of Arcanum Tower, watches the witnesses instead - and counts them.

ch4_testimony.notes: GDD Ch4: uncovered through class-specific approaches, Callen remembers two concrete names - Ashenmere and Greywash. The node stays neutral on method; the fragment surfaces.
text: Under gentle questions Callen comes apart, and what falls out is not confession but geography. A ruin under grey water. A wash of ash. He recites the words like scripture he was made to learn.
Ashenmere. Greywash. Two names, and the room goes quiet around them, because one of them is a place sealed for three hundred years.

choices.label: Say it in front of everyone

ch4_accuse.notes: GDD Ch4: when openly accused, Thessaly confesses - she is a conscious collaborator, serving knowledge, not power. She unleashes forbidden Hollowing magic in the middle of the Council.
text: You say her name and the room turns, and Thessaly laughs - a real laugh, tired and relieved, the laugh of a scholar whose experiment finally reads.
Knowledge, she says. Not power. Somebody has to study the fire while the rest of you argue about smoke. Then she opens the floor of the council chamber, and the Hollowing comes up through it.

ch4_fight.notes: GDD Ch4: Thessaly unleashed, in the middle of the council, on her own terms. Tuned as a hard miniboss (the GDD's boss of the chapter); drops act1_thessaly_cane.
text: Thessaly fights the way she confessed: precisely, and with notes. The Hollowing answers her like a colleague, and the council chambers burn cold.
Three faction leaders are behind you. Fail here and the alliance dies before it is born.

ch4_down.notes: Combat loss recovery for the Thessaly fight. The council guard finishes what you started; the choice about her fate is still yours. Converges on ch4_dilemma.
text: Her third spell takes you off your feet and the fourth goes wide, because the Vigil's guard has arrived, and shields have a geometry no scholar accounts for.
You come up against a pillar with the room still fighting. It is not your blow that brings her down - but the next one after is, and everyone will keep watching you for it.

ch4_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 4 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED outcome is Option A: capture alive - it yields the Choir's complete network inside Arcanum Tower. She is down either way (won the fight, or the council guards pinned her); what is decided is what happens to her next. Both branches converge on ch4_targets.
text: Thessaly is down, breathing hard, one hand still shaping a sigil that no longer has anything behind it. The whole council is watching what you do next.
She is a traitor who chose it with her eyes open, and she is also the only living map of everything the Choir owns inside Arcanum Tower.

choices.label: End her before the spells do

ch4_captured.notes: GDD DETERMINED branch: Option A. Success - Thessaly is subdued, granting the Choir's complete network within Arcanum Tower. Flag ch4_thessaly_captured.
text: You take her wrists in Vigil irons, and she stops fighting, and looks almost grateful. Under interrogation she unfolds the whole network: names, safehouses, dead-drops, in exchange for books.
She asks only for paper. Whatever the Hollowing promised her, what she wanted was to be the one who understood it.

ch4_slain.notes: Non-determined branch: she dies, and the network inside Arcanum Tower stays dark. Written to not contradict the GDD - the two concrete targets still come from Callen's fragments, not from her. Flag ch4_thessaly_slain routes the Chapter 5 approach through the ledger route instead of the interrogation.
text: It is quick, and the council chamber exhales. Magus Oren, her interim successor, will spend months finding what she alone carried and never writes down.
Whatever she served, it did not come for her body. Small mercy, noted by nobody.

ch4_targets.notes: GDD Ch4 outcome: Ashenmere and Greywash become the primary investigation targets before the next full moon; it is also revealed that allies can be collaborators.
text: The council sits late and rises with two names on the order of march. Ashenmere first: the ruins where the Sundering happened, sealed three centuries, now singing again.
Veyra says the other half of the lesson out loud on the stairs: the enemy we found was sitting inside our own council, and she was not possessed. She was hired.

ch4_close.notes: Chapter close. The road to Ashenmere - the original site of the Sundering - and a rest beat before Chapter 5.
text: The road to Ashenmere climbs through country that never recovered. Grey water, grey grass, and stones that were once a city wall, three hundred years done with being anything.
You camp within sight of the quarantine markers, and nobody suggests a fire.

ch5_open.notes: GDD Ch5: Ashenmere, ruins quarantined for 300 years, the original site of The Sundering. Primary node of the Choir network. Objective: investigate it.
text: Ashenmere does not echo. Sound goes into it and does not come back, and your boots make less noise the deeper in you walk.
The ruins are laid out in the same geometry as the sigil at Harrow's Reach, writ city-wide. Somebody designed all of this once, on purpose, at the same table.

ch5_interrogation.notes: GDD Ch5: under interrogation, Thessaly reveals a staggering truth - the Shepherd was one of the seven sorcerers behind the Sundering, now trying to complete what failed. Only reachable via the captured branch; the slain branch re-joins with the guard patrol route below.
text: Thessaly, in irons, trades truth the way other people trade gossip. The Shepherd is not a priest. He is one of the seven - the youngest, whose ritual is still half-finished.
He is not spreading the Hollowing. He is trying to complete something it interrupted. She will not say what, and is visibly afraid of the answer.

ch5_patrol.notes: The slain-branch route into the same facts: a captured Choir quartermaster's ledger carries them instead of Thessaly. Keeps the two dilemma branches on a shared spine without pretending the choice was free.
text: With Thessaly dead, the network she kept in her head stays dead with her - but her quarters in the ruins hold a quartermaster's ledger, and ledgers do not take poison.
The entries are precise and the sums are terrifying. Seven anchor-sites. One already half-fed. A ritual incomplete by one step, three hundred years standing.

ch5_echo.notes: GDD Ch5: in the central chamber, a residual echo replays the failed ritual - revealing the Shepherd's true name, Kaelen, and his motivation: to save a dying loved one.
text: The central chamber keeps the ritual as a scar keeps its cut. Your lamp touches the dais, and it plays: seven figures in a ring. Six old. One young, and shaking.
The young one speaks a name into the dark - Maren - and the dark does not give it back. Then the echo folds up, and the room goes back to waiting.

ch5_core.notes: GDD Ch5: the echo fades, awakening the Sundering Sentinel - a massive ritual-core guardian construct shaped like a pulsing crystal heart. Sets up the dilemma about sealing vs destroying.
text: The core is a heart of crystal the size of a horse, hanging above the dais and beating. Once a minute, and the whole ruin beats with it.
Then it stops beating, and the room gets up. The guardian was not left here to keep people out. It was left to keep the ritual company.

ch5_fight.notes: GDD Ch5: the Sundering Sentinel. Act 1's climax fight - the boss. Drop is act1_sentinel_core. onWin and onLose deliberately diverge: losing here means being carried out of the quarantine with the core still guarded.
text: The Sundering Sentinel comes apart out of the walls - a body built around the core's rhythm, plate over crystal, older than every kingdom on the map.
It does not announce itself. It simply arrives, like weather, and the room is suddenly too small for both of you.

ch5_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: dragged out of the quarantine by the team. The core remains - which is the GDD's DETERMINED outcome (seal, not destroy) reached the hard way.
text: You wake outside the quarantine line with your boots off and your ears still ringing. Dagen carried you the last mile; the Sentinel did not pursue past the dais.
It was never trying to leave. Whatever it guards, it guards in place - and that, Veyra says that night, is the most important thing anyone learned all week.

ch5_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 5 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED outcome is Option B: seal, do not destroy. The Ritual Core is preserved as a major source of knowledge for the Vigil - and remains a target, which drives Acts 2-4 (Ilsevet wants it). Both branches converge on ch5_after.
text: The Sentinel is down and the core is bare: a crystal heart, still beating, with a ritual three centuries old coiled around it like a half-tied knot.
Break it and everything it knows dies with it. Seal it and the Vigil owns the only library of its kind left. And so does whoever comes for it next.

ch5_sealed.notes: GDD DETERMINED branch: Option B. The core is sealed, preserved as a major knowledge source, and remains a valuable target for the future (Act 4's premise). Flag ch5_core_sealed.
text: The Vigil's binding works and the Arcanum's warding works, and neither alone would. The core dims to a slow, banked glow, like a hearth at night.
Veyra leaves a garrison and an order meant to outlive the room: nothing in, nothing out, checked at every moon. You have made Ashenmere a library. Libraries get visited.

ch5_broken.notes: Non-determined branch: the core is destroyed. The knowledge is gone; the ritual with it. Later acts are written so the Choir's remaining fragments and Ilsevet's plan do not depend on the core surviving - but Ashenmere is a ruin instead of a library.
text: It takes everything, and it does not take it quietly. The heart bursts like a struck bell, the note goes out of the world, and the ritual dies in the ringing.
When the dust settles there is nothing on the dais worth carrying. Veyra looks at the empty air where it hung a long time, and says nothing at all.

ch5_after.notes: GDD Ch5 outcome: Kaelen now has a name and a human motive. New clue: an unrecognisable emblem of an extinct order among the original seven sorcerers. Hooks into Ch6.
text: The records you salvage from the chamber agree on two things. The youngest sorcerer was called Kaelen, and he did it for love, and it did not save her.
And on the ring of six, there is a seventh presence the records will not name - an emblem of an order that is not in any of them. Extinct, or erased.

ch6_open.notes: GDD Ch6: the hidden temple of the Ashwardens, deep in Silverleaf Woods. Objective: uncover the complete history of Kaelen and the Ashwardens.
text: Silverleaf does not admit strangers; it tolerates guests. The Wardens meet you at the treeline with bows not quite lowered, and escort you in by paths that refuse to be retraced.
The Ashwardens' temple is not hidden. It is simply uninterested in being found, which is a stronger magic.

ch6_trials.notes: CLASS GATE 1 of 2 in Ch6 (the GDD's three traditional forest trials). Each class passes the trials its own way; the gate node and the three route nodes follow Ch1's structure.
text: Three trials stand between you and the archive: the river that remembers, the dark that listens, and the grove that lies.
Elder Ilyndra Duskwhisper watches from the far side of the water and does not volunteer so much as a syllable. The forest is the teacher here. You are the lesson.

choices.label: Cross the river as it is
Walk the dark by its sounds

ch6_trial_warrior.notes: Warrior trial route. The river that remembers every weight that has crossed it. Honesty through effort.
text: The river takes your weight and adds memory to it - every crossing, every drowning, every grief the water ever carried. You put your head down and carry all of it across.
On the far bank Ilyndra gives you the look a smith gives iron that held its edge. The forest approved, or at least stopped objecting.

ch6_trial_archer.notes: Archer trial route. The dark that listens. You pass by moving like something that belongs to it.
text: The dark listens for fear, so you bring it none. You cross it at the pace of growing things, reading the air by ear, until the dark loses interest like a hound without a scent.
Ilyndra meets you at the edge of the light and says one word in elvish. Dagen does not translate. You walked out of that dark a woods-woman, and it shows.

ch6_trial_mage.notes: Mage trial route. The grove that lies. You answer illusion with grammar until it runs out.
text: The grove shows you your village whole, your family alive, the Hollowing a bad dream. You answer each lie with its cost, out loud, in the old grammar, until the grove runs out of lies to spend.
The trees part like a page turning. Ilyndra is waiting, and her expression has moved somewhere it has not been in a long time.

ch6_ilyndra.notes: GDD Ch6: Ilyndra reveals Kaelen was the youngest apprentice of the Ashwardens, lost his younger sister Maren to an incurable illness, and the Ashwardens held records on siphoning life essence. Five of the six others were driven by ambition.
text: Ilyndra tells it plainly. Kaelen was their youngest apprentice, brilliant, half in love with everything living. His sister Maren sickened, and the archive held answers it should never have held.
Five of the six in that ring wanted power. One wanted his sister back. The Ashwardens have spent three centuries deciding which shames them more.

choices.label: Go down to the deep archive

ch6_archive.notes: GDD Ch6: a guardian echo tests the team's intent before yielding; a brooch bearing a family crest is discovered - identical to Commander Veyra's. Sets up the dilemma.
text: The deep archive is shelved in living wood, and its guardian is a echo of the first Archwarden, who asks what you are looking for and waits for the truth.
You answer. The shelf turns, and behind it hangs a brooch on a thong: a family crest, three hundred years old, and you have seen it every morning on Commander Veyra's collar.

ch6_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 6 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED outcome is Option A: claim full ritual knowledge - it opens the possibility of curing rather than merely defeating Kaelen, which the whole endgame depends on. Both branches converge on ch6_brooch.
text: The shelf offers two things. The complete ritual record, original ashwarden binding, siphoning and unbinding both - everything a cure would need, and everything a massacre would need.
Or a careful summary, truths kept and methods withheld, safe to carry and useless for saving anyone.

ch6_claimed.notes: GDD DETERMINED branch: Option A. The team secures the original ritual records. Flag ch6_ritual_records - Act 2's proof that Kaelen can be saved depends on it.
text: Ilyndra unbuckles the archive's chain herself. The records come out in a wrapped bundle heavier than its size, and the guardian echo reads your intent once more before the door closes.
The Vigil now owns the only complete copy of what broke the world, and of what might mend it. Ilyndra says she will want to know which you use it for.

ch6_summary.notes: Non-determined branch: the summary. History and motive come out the same; the unbinding method does not. Written so Act 2 can still proceed - Kaelen holds the binding half himself, and says so at the watchtower.
text: You leave the deep shelf locked. The summary Ilyndra writes out by hand names Kaelen, names Maren, names the grief - and stops precisely where the working begins.
Safe to carry, she says. Less than the whole truth, you say. She does not disagree, and the door stays shut behind you.

ch6_brooch.notes: GDD Ch6 outcome: the brooch is identical to Veyra's. Ilyndra confirms the crest is Ashwarden. Chapter close, hooking into Ch7.
text: The crest is Ashwarden, Ilyndra says. A family line, not an order rank - one of the households that sheltered the temple's survivors when the Sundering scattered them.
The archive has not been touched by human hands in three centuries, and Commander Veyra wears that crest every day, not knowing what it is. You will be the one to tell her.

ch7_open.notes: GDD Ch7: Greyhold, Veyra's private chambers and secret laboratory. Objective: uncover Veyra's connection to Kaelen and secure the ritual records.
text: Veyra receives the news alone, which is the first strange thing. The second is that she already knew the crest was Ashwarden - she has known since she was six.
She unlocks a door in her own quarters that the plans of Greyhold do not contain. The laboratory behind it is three hundred years of her family asking one question in the dark.

ch7_heirloom.notes: GDD Ch7: the brooch is a family heirloom from an ancestor named Maren who vanished after a great tragedy. Confirmed: Veyra is a direct descendant of Maren, Kaelen's sister who somehow survived.
text: Maren, she says, when she sees it. The name her grandmother would not explain. The line that survived a sickness it should not have, and left, and never said why.
Veyra is Maren's blood. Kaelen's sister lived, and her many-times-great-niece now commands the order hunting him. She sits down slowly, like someone correcting a map.

ch7_night.notes: GDD Ch7: that very night, an agent of the Hollow Choir disguised as kitchen staff attacks Veyra's private quarters the moment her bloodline identity is exposed. Sets up the fight and the dilemma.
text: The warning arrives quietly, as such warnings do. Dagen, in the doorway at midnight, holding up the hand of a kitchen boy he has just hit hard enough to fold.
The boy's sleeve is wrong, and under it the Choir's mark is burned in, and somewhere between the kitchens and this corridor he stopped being a boy at all.

ch7_fight.notes: GDD Ch7: the Choir's agent, come for Veyra the moment her bloodline is exposed. A fast assassin construct. Drop is act1_choir_sigil, taken from its body. onWin and onLose converge on the dilemma, as the GDD's outcome (agent escapes) is decided by the dilemma, not the fight.
text: It comes up off the floor without a face, and the corridor is suddenly all edges. It does not care about you. It cares about the woman behind you, and it is very fast about caring.
Veyra draws behind you. The corridor is four feet wide. Nobody is leaving it politely.

ch7_down.notes: Bridge node: whatever happened in the corridor, the agent is down and the choice is live - hold it here, or let it run and stand by Veyra. Re-joins the GDD spine at the dilemma.
text: The agent is down in the corridor, or driven to its knees with Dagen's knife at the hinge of its jaw. Either way it is not going anywhere in the next ten seconds.
Ten seconds is exactly as long as the fire in the laboratory takes to decide what it wants to be. The archives Veyra pulled tonight are all in there. So is Veyra.

ch7_smoke.notes: Combat loss recovery for the agent fight. The corridor is a draw: the agent is loose, the fire is lit, and the choice is still live. Converges on ch7_dilemma.
text: The agent is quicker than the corridor. It puts you into the wainscoting and steps over you toward the door, and only Dagen - silent, total Dagen - turns it aside long enough for the smoke to decide the rest.
When the air clears you are upright, bleeding, and standing exactly where the chapter's real question was always going to find you.

ch7_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 7 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED outcome is Option A: prioritize Veyra, allow the agent to escape. Veyra is completely safe, but the agent escapes with word that Kaelen's bloodline has been found - the premise of Act 2's ambushes. Both branches converge on ch7_outcome.
text: The agent is slipping its knots, slow and patient, the way its masters built it to. Behind the smoke, the laboratory fire is eating the shelves, and Veyra's voice is still in there.
You cannot do both. Anyone who tells you otherwise has never been in a corridor with one door and two emergencies.

ch7_veyra.notes: GDD DETERMINED branch: Option A. Veyra is completely safe; the agent escapes with word that Kaelen's bloodline has been found. Flag ch7_agent_escaped.
text: You leave the agent and take the door off its hinges instead. Veyra is where the smoke is thickest, arm burned, archives under one arm, alive - the whole of the report that matters.
When you come back out, the corridor is empty. The agent is gone, carrying the only news the Choir wanted: Kaelen's bloodline has been found, and it is her.

ch7_agent_held.notes: Non-determined branch: the agent is held. Veyra saves herself, worse burned, and the laboratory's losses are heavier. Written to not contradict the GDD: the Choir already knows the bloodline - its agent wearing the kitchen mark came ready to report either way.
text: You choose the corridor. It costs the laboratory half a wall and Veyra a forearm she will not feel for a week, and it puts the Choir's agent in irons by dawn.
What it does not cost is the news. The agent was sent to report, not to return; its masters already know what it knows. You have caught a letter that was already read.

ch7_outcome.notes: GDD Ch7 outcome: Veyra is Maren's descendant; Kaelen may never have known his sister lived and had descendants - and now one of them leads the order hunting him. Chapter close with a rest beat.
text: The laboratory burns itself out by morning. The surviving records lie on her table, and Veyra, bandaged, reads them the way other people hold a vigil.
He may never have known, she says, near dawn. That she lived. That the line kept going. And the first thing his people did was send a knife.

ch8_open.notes: GDD Ch8: Veyra receives a midnight vision - Kaelen asks to meet in person at a neutral location in three days, seeking dialogue rather than attack. Respond to the summons via the ancient blood bond.
text: She dreams it standing up, in the middle of the third watch: her eyes open and looking at something a long way off and a long time old.
Kaelen, she says, when she can speak again. He has her eyes, she has Maren's, and he is asking - not summoning, asking - to meet. Alone ground. Three days. The old watchtower on the mist line.

ch8_road.notes: The road to the Old Watchtower, at the edge of the Mist Zone. A rest beat before the Sentinel of the Call.
text: The mist line runs across the country like a scar that has learned patience. The Old Watchtower stands on it, half inside, three days' ride out of Greyhold.
You camp short of the tower, on Vigil ground, with the mist far enough off to be a rumour and close enough to keep the horses awake.

ch8_test.notes: GDD Ch8: en route to the meeting point, the team is intercepted by the Sentinel of the Call, a construct testing peaceful intent versus aggression. Sets up the dilemma.
text: Halfway through the mist the road asks its question. The Sentinel of the Call steps out of it like a verdict: built like the Ashenmere guardian, marked like the Choir's rings, older than both.
It reads what you carry as a customs officer reads manifests. What it finds next is up to you, and it is watching your hands, not your face.

ch8_fight.notes: GDD Ch8: the Sentinel of the Call. It is a test as much as a fight. Drop is act1_watchtower_charm. Either outcome leads to the sheathed-arms decision; the GDD's DETERMINED outcome (small team, weapons sheathed) is the dilemma, not this fight.
text: The Sentinel of the Call does not roar or announce. It simply closes the road, final as a closed question.
Whatever you are about to be, be it now.

ch8_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery with a twist that matches the GDD: the Sentinel is a test, not an executioner. Having bloodied you, it relents - the test was never pass/fail by violence.
text: You come to on the road with the taste of iron and the Sentinel standing over you, waiting, patient as a held breath, for the answer it actually came for.
It did not finish you. It was never going to. It wanted to see what you reached for while falling, and it saw it.

ch8_after_fight.notes: Bridge node: the test is done, the tower is ahead, and the dilemma of how to walk in is live. Re-joins the GDD spine at the dilemma.
text: The Sentinel steps aside, satisfied or indifferent, and the road goes on to the watchtower door. Behind it, something with a heartbeat three centuries old is waiting to talk.
The last hundred yards are the whole of Act One. Everyone with you stops at the threshold and looks at your hands.

ch8_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 8 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED outcome is Option B: enter with a small team, sheathed weapons - complete good faith ahead of the first face-to-face meeting with Kaelen. Both branches converge on the Act 1 ending node.
text: Three days of road, and every one of them has asked the same question. What do you carry into the dark to meet the thing that broke the world - your answer, or your steel?
He asked for dialogue. The Sentinel tested intent. If this is a trap, none has ever been more patient; if not, the first thing he sees will be the truth about you.

ch8_sheathed.notes: GDD DETERMINED branch: Option B. The team demonstrates complete good faith. Flag ch8_arms_sheathed - Act 2's meeting at the watchtower opens on this footing.
text: You unbuckle every blade you own and set them on the road with a hand on top, and the team follows one by one - the only order you ever give that is not a word.
The tower door opens before you reach it. Nobody in three hundred years has walked in to find Kaelen with their hands empty, and he wants that remembered.

ch8_armed.notes: Non-determined branch: you keep your steel. The door still opens - the meeting happens - but the footing is different, and the GDD's good-faith statement is not made. Written to not contradict Act 2.
text: You walk in the way soldiers walk in, and the tower lets you, and that is its own kind of answer.

The figure by the cold hearth looks at your hands longer than your face, and something in the set of his shoulders files the information away. What he wanted to say, he says anyway. What he might have shown you, he does not.

ch8_watchtower_meet.notes: Formerly the Act 1 ending; with Act 2 written this is the rest beat where the telling begins. The GDD's Ch8 outcome holds: battle is not what he seeks. Act 2's real ending is ch16_vision.
text: Kaelen is smaller than the stories, and the stories were built by terrified people. He waits by a dead hearth, hands open, the mist holding the room.
He looks at Veyra a long time. Maren's eyes, he says. Battle is not what he came for - not yet. The telling of three hundred years begins here, and the night is long enough.

ch9_open.notes: GDD Ch9: Kaelen waits alone, without bodyguards - vulnerability as a statement of good faith. He recognizes Maren's eyes in Veyra. The team fights beside him when the mastermind's troops arrive, forging an unspoken alliance. Outcome: Kaelen is no longer the leader of the Choir; the true enemy is an unknown figure pulling strings.
text: He tells it in order, and the order is the confession. Emberfall was not his word. Harrow's Reach was not his word. The Choir stopped being his two centuries ago, and he has been chasing its shadow since.
Veyra listens completely, and asks the only question that matters: who took your movement from you?

ch9_reveal.notes: GDD Ch9: the sealing ritual must be completed at Ashenmere during the Blood Moon - which will kill Kaelen - unless the Ashwarden records hold another way. Mid-conversation, masked troops loyal to the mastermind attack.
text: The sealing must be redone at Ashenmere under the Blood Moon, he says, and the redoing is a death - unless the records you pulled from Silverleaf hold the gentler road he never had.
Then he stops talking, because he is looking at the door. The mist outside has voices in it, and the voices have orders.

ch9_fight.notes: GDD Ch9: masked troops loyal to the mastermind attack mid-conversation; the team fights side by side with Kaelen. A hunter squad, not a duel. Drop is act2_sanctum_tally.
text: They come through the walls the way smoke comes under a door - masked, silent, grey and silver. They do not announce. They were told not to.
Kaelen takes up a sword he has not carried in three centuries and stands where you can see him. It is a kind of trust that does not need saying.

ch9_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: Kaelen carries the team out through mist he has lived in for three centuries. Converges on ch9_after.
text: You wake under stars with the taste of the fight still in you, and Kaelen kneeling over you with three hundred years of knowledge of how to be lost in this mist.
The hunters are gone - called off, not beaten. Somebody knows exactly how the meeting went, and the answer made them stop.

ch9_after.notes: Chapter 9 outcome: alliance forged. Kaelen leads the team to his hidden sanctuary beneath the Old Watchtower.
text: The watchtower has a cellar that is not a cellar. Kaelen takes you down into it, past three centuries of notes pinned floor to ceiling, and closes the world behind you.
The hunters knew where the meeting was. They still lost you in the mist. That is worth more than a victory, and Veyra says so out loud.

ch10_open.notes: GDD Ch10: Kaelen reveals the map of the seven original ritual fragments. Two he secured himself; three are held by the Choir (Duskhollow, Saltmere, the mountain node); the Ashwarden star chart will name the last two. He confirms there may be a way to complete the ritual without dying.
text: The map is the Sundering drawn as an inventory: seven fragments, scattered when it tore. He holds two. The Choir holds three - Duskhollow in the fens, Saltmere under its lighthouse, one under the Concordat's mountains.
The last two are unwritten even here. And the sealing, he says, need not kill him - if the gentle road is real.

ch10_scout.notes: GDD Ch10: a Choir scout is caught infiltrating the sanctuary. Sets up the interrogation choice.
text: Dagen finds the scout before the scout finds anything - wedged behind the note-wall, listening, with a charcoal copy of the fragment map half-finished in his hand.
He is young, terrified, and marked like the kitchen boy at Greyhold: conscripted by something bigger than his fear.

ch10_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 10 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED: capture alive for interrogation. Leaked info: Duskhollow is the least guarded - the logical starting point. Both branches converge on ch10_targets.
text: Alive, he is a leak in the Choir's wall - if he talks, and if what he knows is current. Dead, he is a warning delivered and nothing gained.
The charcoal map in his hand already tells you the Choir believes the fragments are findable. Whether he believes he is going home decides the rest.

choices.label: Turn him loose with a lie

ch10_captured.notes: GDD DETERMINED branch: capture alive. Leaked info: Duskhollow is the least guarded node. Flag ch10_scout_talked.
text: He talks before the tea is cold. Duskhollow is garrisoned by the dying and the desperate; Saltmere by the faithful; the mountain by nobody at all - nobody living walks those tunnels by choice.
Least guarded is not least dangerous, Kaelen says. But it is the place to start, and starting is the whole of what you have.

ch10_released.notes: Non-determined branch: he is released carrying a false target order. Written to not contradict the GDD - the Duskhollow-first facts still arrive, via the copied map his handlers already have.
text: You feed him an order of march that starts anywhere but the fens, and let him climb out into the mist to be a hero to his handlers.
The charcoal copy leaves with him, so the lie has to live inside the truth: Kaelen simply reroutes the real map. Duskhollow remains the door everything opens from.

ch10_targets.notes: GDD Ch10 outcome: three remaining fragments mapped; a real possibility exists to save Kaelen without his death. Chapter close with a rest beat.
text: The plan fits on half a page. Take the three Choir-held fragments, find the last two by star chart, finish the working at Ashenmere under the next Blood Moon - with a road home for the man doing the finishing.
Tonight, for the first time since the Sundering, the map points forward instead of back.

ch11_open.notes: GDD Ch11: Duskhollow Swamps, south of the Mist Zone. Guided by the hermit Old Maddox. Objective: claim the first ritual fragment.
text: The fens breathe. Whole causeways rise and settle like lungs, and the trees lean together overhead to keep the sky out.
Old Maddox finds you before you find him - a hermit with a coracle and three hundred years of the Choir's traffic memorized by the sound of its boots.

ch11_approach.notes: GDD Ch11: the temple is slowly sinking into the marsh, guarded by the Mire Sentinel. The fragment altar is going under - time pressure without a clock.
text: The temple's crown is a rooftop breaking the fen like a drowning man's knuckles. Inside, somewhere below the waterline, the fragment sits on its altar and waits.
Maddox gives it a season, maybe two, before the marsh takes the altar room entirely. The Choir has never minded. Faith does not mind water.

ch11_descent.notes: Sets up the extraction dilemma: forced extraction wakes the Sentinel and floods the chamber; careful extraction is slower and risks the altar going under. GDD DETERMINED is careful extraction - the battle drags but the fragment survives.
text: The flooded nave is waist-deep and lit by fen-light through the cracks. The altar glows under a hand's width of black water, and something enormous breathes somewhere in the dark around it.
Lever it free in one brutal minute and the temple comes down on you at once. Or sing it loose as it was set - slowly, while the water rises.

ch11_fight.notes: GDD Ch11: the Mire Sentinel, a colossal swamp construct. GDD DETERMINED is careful extraction: the battle drags on longer, but the fragment is retrieved intact before the altar submerges. Drop is act2_mire_pearl.
text: The Mire Sentinel unfolds out of the flooded colonnade - peat and stone and older wood, grown over and grown together, patient as the water that built it.
It does not defend the temple. It is the temple's slow dying given fists.

ch11_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: the team is pulled out by Maddox; Kaelen's knowledge finishes the unbinding from the surface. Converges on ch11_recovered.
text: Maddox drags you out by the collar like a drowned calf hauled from a well, and the temple swallows itself behind you.
Kaelen finishes the unbinding from the causeway, hands in the water, reading the fragment up through the murk. The marsh gives it up grudgingly, at dawn.

ch11_recovered.notes: GDD Ch11 outcome: the first fragment is secured; two remain (Saltmere and the mountain node). Flag ch11_fragment_one.
text: The fragment is a hand of black glass that hums against the runestone you carry it in, and the hum is a word you almost know.
One. Two remain. The fens close over the temple behind you without ceremony, and Maddox waves once from his causeway and is gone.

ch12_open.notes: GDD Ch12: Saltmere Fishing Village and the underwater sea cave beneath the Old Lighthouse. Yessa, an old fisherman who lost his child to the lighthouse, warns the team. Objective: retrieve the second fragment.
text: Saltmere smells of tar and herring, and the Old Lighthouse stands at the end of the spit with its lamp long dark and its foundations in the sea cave the village pretends not to know.
Yessa mends his nets with his back to you until you say the word lighthouse. Then he mends nothing, and tells you what the water took from him there.

ch12_cave.notes: GDD Ch12: in the deepest chamber the fragment is guarded by the Brine Sentinel - an ancient whale slowly corrupted by the Hollowing, its eyes reflecting confusion rather than malice. Sets up the purification dilemma.
text: The cave mouth is underwater at high tide and a crawl at low; inside, the sea has spent ten thousand years carving a cathedral.
In the deepest chamber the fragment glows on its stone shelf. Around it something vast and slow sings wrong - a whale, old and grey, wearing the Hollowing. Its eyes are not cruel. They are lost.

ch12_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 12 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED: purify the creature using ritual knowledge rather than kill it - the first empirical proof the Hollowing can be reversed, and strong evidence Kaelen can be saved. Both branches converge on ch12_after.
text: Kill it and the fragment is retrievable in minutes; the cave stays quiet; and the first proof that any of this can be undone dies with the whale.
Purify it and you are doing surgery in the dark on something the size of a chapel, with the sea for blood. The Ashwarden records say it can be done. Records also sink.

choices.label: Put it down and take it

ch12_fight.notes: GDD Ch12: the Brine Sentinel. Under the purify branch (DETERMINED) the fight is the purification - the team holds it in the working while the Hollowing is drawn out, and it ends confused, clean, and free. Drop is act2_brine_scale.
text: The Brine Sentinel fills the chamber end to end. The Hollowing speaks through its song, and the song shakes silt from the ceiling in ropes.
Whatever you came to do, you do it here, in its dark, on its terms.

ch12_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: the sea gives the team back at low tide; Kaelen completes the working from the shallows. Converges on ch12_after.
text: The cave spits you out with the tide, half-drowned and empty-handed, and the whale's song follows you back to the village - thinner now, like something calling across a growing distance.
Kaelen stands waist-deep in the shallows until dawn, singing the Ashwarden half of the working. At first light the song from the cave changes key.

choices.label: Go back in with the light

ch12_purified.notes: GDD Ch12 outcome: the whale purified - the first empirical proof that the Hollowing can be reversed, not just destroyed. Flag ch12_whale_purified (checked at Act 4's Ilsevet refusal echo).
text: It comes out of the Hollowing the way a sleeper surfaces from a nightmare - flinch, breath, and then enormous quiet. The grey sheds off it in sheets and drifts down like snow.
Its eyes clear. It looks at you - at Kaelen longest - and the cave sings a chord nobody taught it. Proof, in a hundred tons of whale: the Hollowing comes out.

ch12_after.notes: GDD Ch12 outcome: second fragment secured. Flag ch12_fragment_two.
text: Two fragments ride in the runestone now, humming their almost-word to each other. The village meets you at the tide line with every boat lit like a festival.
Yessa touches the lighthouse stones on his way past, once, as you touch a grave - or the start of letting one be.

ch13_open.notes: GDD Ch13: the team's secret plans leak to the Choir - there is a spy inside Greyhold. The suspect is an Iron Concordat soldier, Bryn.
text: The leak is undeniable by its shape: the Choir knew the watchtower meeting, and now somebody knows the fragment count. The circle of who could is small.
It is one soldier wide. Bryn, of the Concordat detachment - present at the council, at the muster, and nowhere near the watchtower, which is exactly how a careful spy stands still.

ch13_truth.notes: GDD Ch13: Bryn is a victim, not a willing traitor - his family is held hostage by the Choir as leverage.
text: He does not deny a word of it. He unbuttons his cuff instead, and shows you the burn of the Choir's mark, and hands over the letters that bought him.
A wife in Hollow's Reach. Two children. The letters are in his wife's hand, and every sentence in them is hers, and none of them were written free.

ch13_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 13 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED: rescue Bryn's family unharmed, even though the hostage overseer escapes with minor intel. Both branches converge on ch13_after.
text: The Choir expects its leverage used. The letters include a drop schedule; the family can be taken quietly in a night that risks the overseer bolting with what he knows - or the handoff can be played to trap him, spending the family's safety as the stake.
Bryn asks for the first with his eyes on the floor. He does not ask twice.

ch13_family.notes: GDD DETERMINED branch: family rescued unharmed; the hostage overseer escapes with minor additional intel. Flag ch13_family_safe. Outcome: Bryn rehabilitated, fiercely loyal - he volunteers as purification test subject in Ch20.
text: The rescue is four hours of borrowed carts and a fish-wagon nobody searches twice. The family comes out unharmed; the overseer escapes with nothing to report but noise.
Bryn does not thank you. He reports for duty an hour later with his letter-burn turned toward the fire, and from that day the Concordat detachment follows you on sight.

ch13_trap.notes: Non-determined branch: the overseer is taken, but the family escapes in the confusion and the Choir moves them beyond reach. Written to not contradict the GDD - Bryn still turns loyal, from a colder place.
text: The trap wins the overseer, whose ledger of hostage houses is worth a company of soldiers - and loses the family, moved beyond every border you can name when it sprang.
Bryn sees the ledger's value before he sees the cost. He reports the same hour, quieter, and follows you after that like a man paying in instalments.

ch13_after.notes: GDD Ch13 outcome: the Choir now knows the team heads for the mountain node. Rest beat before Ch14.
text: The mountain fragment cannot wait on a perfect plan: the scout knew, so the Choir knows, and a head start is only worth having before the opposition arrives.
Harwick sends word from the Concordat: his sappers will meet you at the old Dwarf mine. He is bringing more than shovels, the letter says, and he does not apologize for it.

ch14_open.notes: GDD Ch14: Kaelen's sanctuary, then the Ashwarden temple. Ilyndra confirms a gentler version of the ritual, never tested. An Elven star chart locates the last two fragments: Sky Sanctum and the Cinder Wastes. Objective: ensure the purification ritual can truly save Kaelen.
text: Ilyndra receives the whole story - fragments, whale, Kaelen alive and cooperating - standing very still, hands folded, as one does among fragile things.
Then she opens the star chart kept against this exact need. Two lights remain: Sky Sanctum, in Silverleaf's highest canopy, and the Cinder Wastes, at the heart of the Mist Zone.

ch14_trial.notes: GDD Ch14: a small-scale trial of the purification ritual spins out of control; DETERMINED is stabilizing it together rather than aborting. Sets up the trial fight: the working itself manifests a lash of wild aether.
text: The trial is one candle, one bowl of water, one grain of the Hollowing siphoned from a warding jar. It lights. It grows. Within a minute it is a lash of grey fire looking for something to be.
Abort, and months of road end in a scorched bench. Hold it, and the thing in the bowl has to be carried by every hand in the room at once.

ch14_fight.notes: GDD Ch14: the trial's wild aether - not an enemy so much as the ritual testing everyone holding it. GDD DETERMINED: the team stabilizes it together; complete success. No drop (it dissolves); the EXP is the lesson.
text: The lash takes shape out of the bowl - grey fire with a memory of intention, testing each grip on it the way floodwater tests a wall.
Ilyndra marks the working's rhythm with a bell. Your part is to give the fire exactly what it wants, at exactly the wrong moment, forever.

ch14_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: the trial is doused, the team is burned but wiser; Ilyndra re-cuts the working and the second attempt holds. Converges on ch14_proven.
text: The lash is doused in the bowl's own water and the bench is a char and your hands are burned in a lattice you will read like a map for weeks.
Ilyndra does not scold. She re-cuts the working with two changes her grandmother's books insisted on, and the second attempt holds like a well-behaved animal.

ch14_proven.notes: GDD Ch14 outcome: the Purification Ritual is proven viable in theory and small-scale practice; all seven fragments are fully mapped. Flag ch14_ritual_proven. Flag ch14_fragments_mapped.
text: Seven lights on one map now: two in Kaelen's keeping, three taken back, two named by stars. And one working, proven small, that takes the Hollowing out of a living thing without killing it.
Kaelen looks at the bowl for a long time - at a thing that worked - and lets himself, for exactly one breath, look like a man who might live.

ch15_open.notes: GDD Ch15: an old Dwarf mine fortified as a Choir stronghold. General Harwick leads the assault, admitting his past doubts were mistaken. The fragment is now far more heavily guarded - the leak in Ch13 told the Choir the team was coming.
text: The mine is three levels down and garrisoned like a keep. The leak bought the Choir weeks to fortify, and they spent every one of them.
Harwick stands at the mouth of it with his whole command and says, in front of witnesses, that he was wrong about you - which from Harwick is a speech, a coronation, and an apology at once.

ch15_breach.notes: GDD Ch15: Choir elite troops threaten to collapse the tunnels where local Dwarf miners are trapped. Sets up the dilemma: miners first vs fragment first.
text: The gate falls, and the Choir's answer is the mine itself: fire-pots laid in the supports, and a voice from below counting down a promise to bring three levels of mountain down.
The tunnels below still hold Dwarf miners - the old workings never emptied, they just stopped being spoken to. The fragment altar is two levels down, past them.

ch15_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 15 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED: prioritize saving the miners despite making the battle tougher. Both branches converge on ch15_fight.
text: Save the miners and you fight the elite on ground they chose, in the dark they prepared, at strength they did not expect you to grant them.
Go for the fragment first and the miners become the argument the Choir makes to everyone who ever considers standing with the Vigil. Harwick will follow either order. He will only respect one.

ch15_fight.notes: GDD Ch15: the Choir's elite warden holding the altar level. Harwick fights alongside the team - the Concordat is now a full ally. Drop is act2_mine_tally.
text: The warden holds the altar gallery like a bishop holds a cathedral: armoured, fanatical, and freshly certain of paradise.
Harwick's shield-line anchors the tunnel mouth. The middle of the room belongs to you.

ch15_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: Harwick's line holds and the warden is brought down by weight of arms after you fall. Converges on ch15_recovered.
text: You wake against a timber support with Harwick's boot in your ribs, keeping you upright as he keeps everything - by leaning on it.
The warden went down to the shield-wall in the end. The fragment was already in the runestone when you stood, which is the Concordat's whole manner of fighting in one sentence.

ch15_recovered.notes: GDD Ch15 outcome: the third Choir-held fragment is secured; the Iron Concordat is now a fully unconditional ally. Flag ch15_fragment_three. Flag ch15_concordat_ally.
text: Three fragments hum in the runestone now, and the mine rings with Dwarf voices that have not been loud in a generation.
Harwick signs the alliance as a man signs his own name, and the Concordat's war-host is yours to call from this hour forward.

ch16_open.notes: GDD Ch16: the puppet master finally reveals herself. A collective vision intrusion - a figure in black and silver: Ilsevet Cray, the unmentioned seventh sorceress, the true architect. Objective: survive the vision and the attack that rides it.
text: She comes for the whole camp at once, in the space behind your eyes: black and silver, ageless, amused. The seventh sorceress - the one the histories were edited to forget.
Ilsevet Cray, she says, into every mind at Greyhold. Kaelen was always weak - too blinded by love to understand that the Hollowing is not a curse. It is evolution.

ch16_enforcer.notes: GDD Ch16: a trusted enforcer of Ilsevet attacks Greyhold while the vision takes place. Drop is act2_enforcer_gauntlet. onLose diverges: the enforcer escapes into the Mist Zone with Greyhold's measure.
text: The vision is the diversions; the attack is the point. Her enforcer walks out of the Mist Gate through Greyhold's prepared defences as though they had been described to him in advance.
He is the finest thing she has ever built, and he has come to measure the fortress that keeps interfering.

ch16_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: the enforcer disengages on a schedule, satisfied. Converges on ch16_after_fight.
text: He puts you down almost gently, as one sets a compass on a table, and walks the walls for exactly as long as it takes to count them.
Then he leaves as he came, through the Mist Gate, unhurried. The measurement was the mission. Greyhold passed it or failed it - that is her question now.

choices.label: Rise and read what it meant

ch16_after_fight.notes: Bridge node: the enforcer is beaten or gone; the dilemma of protecting civilians versus the enforcer's escape is live. Re-joins the GDD spine at the dilemma.
text: Smoke stands over the lower town in columns, and the enforcer's shape is somewhere inside it - walking out slowly, or holding a street, or both.
Greyhold's civilians are in the streets because night bells are not a language they have learned yet. You cannot be in two places, and the smoke knows it.

ch16_dilemma.notes: THE CHAPTER 16 DILEMMA. GDD DETERMINED: prioritize protecting Greyhold's civilians completely, allowing the enforcer to escape. Both branches converge on ch16_vision, the Act 2 ending.
text: Catch the enforcer and Greyhold learns what its bells cost. Shield the streets and the best construction of Ilsevet's long age walks out of your fortress with her questions answered.
Veyra puts it in one line, her hand already on the bells: walls can be rebuilt from inside. People cannot.

ch16_civilians.notes: GDD DETERMINED branch: civilians protected completely; the enforcer escapes. Flag ch16_enforcer_escaped. Outcome: the true enemy has a face and a name; Act 2 concludes.
text: You spend the night being where the bells say, and Greyhold learns the bells. Not one civilian dies in her general's first audit of the fortress.
The enforcer walks out before dawn, her name in every mouth by noon: Ilsevet Cray. The true enemy has a face, a name, and an appointment - with the Ritual Core, under the Blood Moon.

choices.label: End the act on the wall

ch16_pursued.notes: Non-determined branch: the enforcer is driven into the mist but not taken; Greyhold's civilians pay in dead. Written to not contradict the GDD - he still escapes with the same measure, and the name still spreads.
text: You catch him at the Mist Gate and put him into the mist bleeding, which should have been a triumph and was only arithmetic: for every wound, a street without you.
He goes into the mist alive, and Greyhold buries nineteen of its own by noon. The fortress knows her name now - Ilsevet Cray - paid for at a rate nobody stops counting.

choices.label: End the act on the wall

ch16_vision.notes: Act 2 close / bridge to Act 3, per the GDD's Ch16 outcome: the enemy has a face and a name. reward_modifier scales the simulated payout; leaderboard_tag buckets the run.
text: From the wall, the fires, the grey edge of the Mist Zone and the road south read as one country - and the woman who means to own it has finally shown her face.
Ilsevet Cray. Seventh sorceress, emptied record, architect. Greyhold does not mourn; Greyhold musters. The summons goes out to Dawnhold and Silverleaf before the fires are cold.

ch17_open.notes: GDD Ch17 open: Greyhold's Council Chamber, three banners, Magus Oren offering Arcanum Tower's unconditional cooperation after Thessaly.
text: Greyhold's council chamber has never held three banners before. The Vigil keeps a neutral table out of habit; tonight it holds an alliance in the making.
Magus Oren, interim head of Arcanum Tower, stands where Thessaly stood. He offers everything his order has, and asks only to be allowed to help.

ch17_oren.notes: GDD Ch17: Oren offers Arcanum's registry - rites, wards, seven centuries of Sundering notes - as his order's penance.
text: "Thessaly was mine to watch," Oren says, before you can decide how to ask. "I watched her badly. Arcanum's penance is therefore Arcanum's to spend."
He unrolls the order's full registry - rites, wards, seven centuries of notes on the Sundering - and signs it over to Greyhold's table without a counter-clause.

ch17_delegates.notes: GDD Ch17: the three delegations take the neutral table; Ilsevet's assassins are already inside the mountain.
text: Harwick argues like a wall being built - course by course, load tested. Silverleaf's Warden-Envoy argues like weather. Oren argues like a man reading a ledger he has already confessed in.
The oath is drafted by midnight. Somewhere below, in corridors the Vigil has not swept since the Sundering, four of Ilsevet's killers count doors.

ch17_fight.notes: GDD Ch17: Ilsevet's assassins strike during the summit. One shade reaches the chamber; the rest are the dilemma. Drop is act3_ashen_scout.
text: The oath dies mid-word. A shade unfolds from the chimney shadow above the table - grey and silver, dressed to match a mistress who signs nothing.
It moves for the delegation. You move faster.

ch17_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: the Vigil's guards bring the shade down after you fall. Converges on ch17_protect.
text: You wake against the neutral table with the oath spilled across it and a Vigil boot holding your shoulder down, gently, like a question.
The shade is dead on the floor - the guards finished it. Its knife is already in an evidence jar, and its brothers are already moving.

ch17_protect.notes: GDD Ch17 Dilemma - DETERMINED: protect all three faction leaders equally; none may be sacrificed. Three parallel routes converge on ch17_aftermath.
text: The shade was the needle. The threat is the seam: three leaders, three wings of the mountain, one strike team splitting to meet them.
You cannot be three places. The Vigil's maps say you can be one place faster than anyone.

ch17_harwick.notes: GDD Ch17 determined route: the Concordat wing is held. No leader is sacrificed.
text: You take the Deep Road two turns ahead of the killers and arrive with your back to Harwick's chair, which is where you wanted to be when they came.
They came. It went badly for them. Harwick does not thank you; he signs faster, which among Dwarves is the higher compliment.

ch17_envoy.notes: GDD Ch17 determined route: the Silverleaf wing is held. No leader is sacrificed.
text: The Envoy's wing smells of nightbloom and, under it, of ash that has no source. You follow the ash.
Two killers reach her door and learn what a Warden-Envoy's bodyguard does with a corridor. You do the arithmetic in advance; nobody dies.

ch17_oren_wing.notes: GDD Ch17 determined route: the Arcanum wing is held. No leader is sacrificed.
text: Oren's wing is silent when you reach it - the bad kind of silent, the kind Thessaly taught this mountain to distrust.
You break the silence first. Two shades go down under ward-light and steel before either of them finishes a syllable of their mistress's name.

ch17_aftermath.notes: GDD Ch17 outcome: no leader harmed, the oath completes. Flag ch17_alliance.
text: The mountain settles. Three leaders stand unharmed at one table, which is exactly what Ilsevet sent four killers to prevent.
The oath is finished before dawn, in full, with all names spoken. What is sworn on the neutral table of the Vigil binds all who hear it.

ch17_sealed.notes: GDD Ch17 close: the Three-Faction Alliance is formed; joint strike teams depart for Sky Sanctum and the Cinder Wastes. Bridge to Ch18.
text: Two strike teams go out with the morning: one to the highest canopy of Silverleaf, one into the Cinder Wastes' grey heart. You will lead the first and meet the second at Ashenmere.
Harwick salutes with his hammer. Oren salutes with his ledger. The Envoy simply nods, which from her is a parade.

ch18_open.notes: GDD Ch18 open: the ascent to Sky Sanctum, highest canopy of Silverleaf; the sixth fragment's keeper walks above.
text: The mist around Silverleaf's crown is not weather; it is breath. Something that large up there inhales, and a thousand leaves lean with it.
The Canopy Guardian was planted to keep this place. The Hollowing has kept it instead, and worn the warden's shape as water wears a stair.

ch18_survey.notes: GDD Ch18 optional beat: reading the guardian's patterns from below before the climb.
text: From the ground you read the guardian as Oren taught you to read wards: where it stands, what it spares, what it has already given up protecting.
It never strikes the young trees. Whatever wears it still knows the difference between a forest and an obstacle. That is worth knowing before you climb.

ch18_ascent.notes: GDD Ch18: the climb through silver mist; roots bar the last span.
text: The climb is three hours of wet rope and older wood. The mist rises with you, patient as tide, and where it touches your sleeves the thread goes grey.
On the last span the guardian's roots bar the way like a portcullis that grew. Beyond them, the sanctum's crown glows a colour light should not make.

ch18_guardian.notes: GDD Ch18: the Canopy Guardian revealed; Saltmere's technique is the plan, per the GDD's call-back to Ch12.
text: It rises out of its own roots like a hillside deciding to stand: bark gone the grey of the Mist Zones, sap gone dark, a face it should not have and does.
Beneath the rot the warden it was is still visible - the way Saltmere's whale was still a whale. The technique is the one that worked on the sea. It must work in the air.

ch18_fight.notes: GDD Ch18: the Canopy Guardian fight - the DETERMINED outcome is purification, not destruction; winning is the purifying. Drop is act3_canopy_seed.
text: The warden fights as a forest argues with a storm: slowly, then all at once, from every side at once.
Your team works the canopy lanes while you hold its attention. Every clean cut is not damage - it is a line of the working, drawn in sap and salt.

ch18_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: the team finishes the working after you fall. Converges on ch18_purify.
text: You wake in a nest of rope and leaves with a ranger's hand on your chest and the sound of something enormous weeping sap.
