The team finished the working without you. That is what you built the team for, though it never gets easier to be the reason they needed to.

ch18_purify.notes: GDD Ch18 Dilemma - DETERMINED: purify, never destroy; flawless execution. Flag ch18_canopy_purified.
text: The last line of the working closes over the guardian's heart like a hand closing over a coal. Saltmere's whale surfaced into clean water; the guardian roots into clean light.
Grey drains out of the bark like a fever breaking. It kneels - a hillside, kneeling - and the mist stops being weather.

ch18_restored.notes: GDD Ch18 outcome: the ancient tree restored; Sky Sanctum opens to the team.
text: The sanctum's crown opens like a hand. Inside, Light that predates the Sundering falls across a platform of living wood, and the Warden-Envoy finally, briefly, smiles.
The guardian stands whole at the rim of the light, warden again, and inclines its crown to let you pass.

ch18_fragment.notes: GDD Ch18 outcome: the sixth fragment is secured; only Cinder Wastes remains. Flag ch18_fragment_six. Bridge to Ch19.
text: The guardian gives the sixth fragment the way a warden returns a misdelivered letter: relieved of the weight, sorry it was ever carried here.
Six hum in the runestone now. One remains, and it waits in the grey heart of the Cinder Wastes - in Ilsevet's own house.

ch19_open.notes: GDD Ch19 open: the deepest heart of the Mist Zone, Ilsevet's main fortress. Two approaches read differently.
text: The Cinder Wastes do not end; they arrive. Ash hangs without wind, and the fortress ahead is built from the same grey, as if the land was asked for a keep and obliged.
This is the seventh fragment's prison, and the front door of the woman who means to reverse everything you are about to fix.

ch19_prisoner.notes: GDD Ch19: a captured Choir lieutenant leaks Ilsevet's master plan - seize the Ritual Core at Ashenmere during the Blood Moon and reverse it to spread the Hollowing realm-wide.
text: The Choir lieutenant taken at the gate talks before the second question, as men do when the thing they served stopped pretending to be a faith.
Her mistress's plan, whole: the Core sealed beneath Ashenmere in the spring, reopened at the Blood Moon - turned inside out to pour the Hollowing across the realm instead of closing it.

ch19_vision.notes: GDD Ch19: Ilsevet appears, mocking Kaelen through a vision, then departs for Ashenmere ahead of the team. Flag ch19_vision_seen.
text: She meets you in the ash as her assassins do: already there, courteous. The vision wears her exactly - grey, silver, patient.

"Three centuries, brother-in-failure," she says, "and you still bargain with ghosts. I keep the real things." His answer is to take the vision apart line by line - its own contempt - and she leaves laughing.

ch19_fight.notes: GDD Ch19: the fortress's last warden guards the fragment vault. Drop is act3_warden_plate.
text: The vault's warden has stood since before the fortress was finished, and the Hollowing has had three centuries to perfect it.
It does not guard the fragment for Ilsevet. It guards it because that is the only order left inside it that still burns.

ch19_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: the strike team's weight of arms brings the warden down after you fall. Converges on ch19_vault.
text: You wake in the vault doorway with the team's shields locked over you like a roof.
The warden kneels in defeat, unmade by the same patience it was built from. The vault stands open.

ch19_vault.notes: GDD Ch19 Dilemma - DETERMINED: secure the fragment safely over recklessly pursuing Ilsevet. Restraint now is what arrives at Ashenmere with an army later. Flag ch19_fragment_seven.
text: The seventh fragment hums in its cradle, and the road south - the one Ilsevet took - stands open and taunting. The runestone could hold all seven tonight. The pursuit could cost you everything tonight instead.
Kaelen weighs it aloud, and for once the ghost sounds young. You give the order he cannot: the fragment first. The hunt keeps.

ch20_open.notes: GDD Ch20 open: Greyhold's emergency ritual hall, all seven fragments, a full-scale trial before the march to Ashenmere.
text: Greyhold's ritual hall has not been used at full scale since the Sundering it was built to study. Tonight the seven fragments sit in their cradles like a sentence waiting for its verb.
Oren's mages chalk the working in silver. Kaelen circles the circle, reading his own masterpiece three centuries older, and says nothing for a long time.

ch20_kaelen.notes: GDD Ch20: Kaelen feels true hope for the first time in three centuries.
text: "I built this to close a wound," Kaelen says, "and it has been three hundred years of watching the wound learn."

He touches the edge of the chalk circle without entering it. "Tonight it is only a trial, and I am afraid of a trial. Do you understand what that hope costs a man like me?" You tell him you are beginning to.

ch20_bryn.notes: GDD Ch20: Bryn - saved in Ch13, still carrying traces of corruption - volunteers as the trial's subject. Flag referenced by Act 1's ch13_family_safe.
text: Bryn volunteers before anyone can ask. The mine overseer's shadow still sits in the boy's eyes - traces the Hollowing left that no one has been able to scrub.
"You pulled me out," Bryn says simply. "If the ritual keeps anyone else from needing pulling out, use me first."
Kaelen looks at the boy like a man pricing his own conscience.

ch20_trial.notes: GDD Ch20: the trial - the ritual itself is the encounter; the corruption resists purification like an enemy. Winning is Bryn made whole. Drop is none.
text: The working takes Bryn the way a river takes a swimmer: gently, then entirely. The corruption does not surrender. It litigates.
You and Kaelen hold the lines of the ritual while it argues. This is what the fragments were carved for. Hold.

ch20_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: Kaelen and Oren's mages hold the working after you fall. Converges on ch20_clean.
text: You come to on the hall's cold stone with Kaelen's voice above you, still counting the lines of the ritual like a heartbeat.
The working held without you. Kaelen built it to hold alone; it only needed someone to believe it would.

ch20_clean.notes: GDD Ch20 Dilemma - DETERMINED: accept Bryn's offer with extreme care; he recovers completely, proving the ritual safe for human subjects. Flag ch20_bryn_healed.
text: The last grey thread leaves Bryn's eyes at moonset, and the boy sneezes, which is somehow the proof everyone needed.
The ritual is safe for human subjects. The word human is doing the heaviest work in that sentence, and Kaelen hears it, and stands straighter for it.

ch20_ready.notes: GDD Ch20 close: the Purification Ritual is ready; the team sets out for Ashenmere. Bridge to Ch21.
text: The army moves at dawn in three columns that were one enemy's worth of grudges a season ago. The runestone rides with Kaelen, and the fragments sing to each other quietly, like a choir tuning.
Bryn marches with the Dwarf column, clean-eyed, carrying a standard. The boy you pulled out of a mine is now a flag the army follows.

ch21_open.notes: GDD Ch21 open: the mountain pass to Ashenmere is blocked by waves of Hollowed; the shortcut must be broken open in time.
text: The mountain pass is the difference between arriving at Ashenmere before the Blood Moon or watching it rise over an unbreached wall.
It is also full. The Hollowed come up the switchbacks in waves, drawn to the runestone like moths that have forgotten what they loved about light.

ch21_push.notes: GDD Ch21: Kaelen insists on clearing the shortcut alone; Veyra refuses to let him shoulder it by himself.
text: Kaelen means to take the vanguard alone - three centuries of practising grief have made him efficient at carrying things by himself.
Veyra does not argue. She simply steps into the line beside him and starts giving orders in the voice of a woman who has buried a family and declines to bury another. He yields to that.

ch21_fight.notes: GDD Ch21: breakthrough fight - the team fights alongside Kaelen, minimising his strain (the DETERMINED outcome). Drop is none.
text: The pass narrows to a throat, and the Hollowed come down it like a landslide with opinions.
You and Veyra take the flanks so Kaelen only has to hold the line - shared weight, which is the whole argument of this act in one tactical decision.

ch21_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: the army's weight clears the pass after you fall. Converges on ch21_opened.
text: You wake on a litter on the far side of the pass with the sound of an army marching through a gap that no longer has teeth.
Kaelen cleared the throat after you fell. Veyra's orders were still in his ears when he did it, which is the only reason he was able to.

ch21_opened.notes: GDD Ch21 outcome: the path opens on time; Kaelen grows visibly weaker - urgency rises. Flag ch21_pass_open. Bridge to Ch22.
text: The pass opens on schedule, and Kaelen leans on his staff in a way he would never lean on a person.
He is weaker - visibly, undeniably - and every hour of the march south is now measured against what he has left to spend.

ch22_open.notes: GDD Ch22 open: the combined encampment outside Ashenmere, the night before the Blood Moon.
text: The camp outside Ashenmere holds more banners than some kingdoms own: Concordat iron, Silverleaf green, Arcanum's grey-silver, and the Vigil's plain grey above them all.
Tomorrow night the moon rises red. Tonight the camp smells of woodsmoke, oiled steel, and forty kitchens arguing about seasoning.

ch22_campfire.notes: GDD Ch22: the campfire moment - Kaelen apologises for Emberfall and Harrow's Reach, though they were not his orders; Veyra forgives him fully on behalf of the family.
text: At the largest fire, Kaelen apologises for Emberfall and Harrow's Reach - atrocities done by the thing that borrowed his name, in his voice, with his hands.
Veyra forgives him fully, on behalf of a family that never got to argue with him properly. "Grieve with us," she says. "Not instead of us." The fire pops.

ch22_scouts.notes: GDD Ch22 Dilemma - DETERMINED: subdue Ilsevet's advance scouts silently, without raising a general alarm; the element of surprise is preserved. Flag ch22_silent.
text: Ilsevet's advance scouts prowl the pickets - reading the camp, counting columns, ready to report a warning south that would cost the whole war its edge.
The determined way is the quiet way: subdue them without one general alarm, and the Blood Moon rises over an enemy who thinks she is ahead.

ch22_end.notes: GDD Ch22 close: final plan set, morale high, surprise preserved. Flag ch22_plan_set. Bridge to Ch23.
text: The scouts wake bound and gagged in a supply tent, retired from espionage by people who were gentler about it than their mistress deserved.
The final plan goes round the fires by word of mouth: the assault at dusk, the Core before moonrise. Morale is high. Surprise is intact. The moon does not know yet.

ch23_open.notes: GDD Ch23 open: breaching Ashenmere's outer defenses with the combined army at dusk.
text: Dusk, and the army goes in with the moon rising wrong - red gathering at its rim like a bruise.
Harwick's shield-wall, Silverleaf's bows, Oren's wards: three war machines that have never moved together move together, and Ashenmere's outer defences learn what that costs.

ch23_gate.notes: GDD Ch23: another of Ilsevet's Vessels guards the inner gate.
text: The inner gate has a keeper. It was a person once - you can tell by how it stands, how it holds its arms, everything except the eyes.
Ilsevet's Vessels are her masterpiece: Hollowed bodies carrying trained minds, pain held at arm's length and used as fuel. This one salutes its mistress's door.

ch23_fight.notes: GDD Ch23: the Vessel at the inner gate - the DETERMINED outcome is purification, executed with now-matured technique. Drop is act3_vessel_tear.
text: The Vessel fights like grief with a sword: fluent, practised, and aiming somewhere past you at everything it has lost.
The working goes in with the blades now - the team no longer needs telling. This is what three acts of refusing the easy kill buys.

ch23_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: the army's mages complete the purification after you fall. Converges on ch23_purify.
text: You wake against the gatehouse with ward-light still crawling over your hands and the Vessel kneeling in the wreckage of its orders.
Oren's mages finished the working. The gate stands open. The army flows around you like water around a stone.

ch23_purify.notes: GDD Ch23 Dilemma - DETERMINED: purify the Vessel instead of killing it - smooth, mature technique. Flag ch23_vessel_purified.
text: The Vessel comes back to itself on its knees, weeping, human, alive - the third proof that this war can be won without a single necessary monster.
Kaelen looks longest. Every purification is a door he thought was bricked shut, opening.

ch23_gate_open.notes: GDD Ch23 outcome: outer defenses crumble; the road to the Ritual Core lies open. Bridge to Ch24.
text: Ashenmere's outer ring falls by moonrise, and the city that sealed your first great victory opens its dark streets downward, toward the Core.
The Blood Moon is two hours from full. Ilsevet is somewhere below, with three centuries of patience and one borrowed night.

ch24_open.notes: GDD Ch24 open: the Ritual Core chamber; the first verbal confrontation between Kaelen and Ilsevet in three centuries.
text: The Ritual Core chamber is a dome of sealed light with a crack in it where a woman is standing, and she does not look up when the doors give.
Kaelen speaks her name, three hundred years unsaid. "Ilsevet." She replies without turning: "Brother-failure. You brought children to a hanging."

ch24_pursue.notes: GDD Ch24 dilemma alternate route: the reckless pursuit is checked - the seal cannot be left half-stabilised, so the outcome converges on the DETERMINED one (secure the Core first).
text: You are three steps into the dark after her before Kaelen's voice stops you - not an order, worse: arithmetic. "The seal holds because two of us hold it. Leave, and it unbinds behind you."
You come back to the circle. She wanted the pursuit; the discipline denies her an easy trap, and the working closes on schedule.

ch24_throne.notes: GDD Ch24: Ilsevet reveals her own wound - not a loss born of love like Kaelen's, but being ignored and deemed weak by the other five sorcerers.
text: "You lost a sister," she says to Kaelen, still not turning. "I lost an audience. Five sorcerers looked at me and saw weather - something to be endured, never consulted."
"The Hollowing looked." The crack in the seal widens as she speaks, patient as a door. "The Hollowing was the first thing in this world to find me interesting."

ch24_final_core.notes: Act 3 close / bridge to Act 4, per the GDD's Ch24 outcome: the Core is fully secured and Ilsevet flees deeper into Ashenmere; the Blood Moon rises tonight. Act 4 (duel, blood anchor, healing) opens from here.
text: She flees deeper as the seal closes - not beaten, scheduled. The Core steadies, the light goes from cracked gold to whole, and Kaelen exhales three centuries at once.
The Blood Moon reaches full over Ashenmere. Below, the last sorceress of the Sundering waits, and for the first time in this war the next step is the last one.

ch25_open.notes: GDD Ch25 open: the inner corridors of Ashenmere under the rising Blood Moon; the descent to Ilsevet's throne.
text: Below the Core, the corridors are older than the city that built them - Sundering-era stone, drinking the red light and giving nothing back.
Kaelen walks point. Half his body has gone black and veined like cracked glass; three centuries of holding the door shut from the inside, written on him at last.

ch25_soldiers.notes: GDD Ch25: young coalition soldiers nearly attack Kaelen out of panic; Veyra defends him.
text: The panic starts small - a young Concordat spear, then two, then a whole landing braced against the walls with their eyes on the cracking man leading you.
Veyra steps into the spear-line without breaking stride. "He has held back this darkness for all of us," she says, "for three centuries. Lower them." They lower them.

ch25_guard.notes: GDD Ch25 Dilemma - DETERMINED: protect Kaelen while calming the allied troops; trust grows. Flag ch25_trust.
text: You put yourself between Kaelen and the longest spear in the room and give the soldiers the one thing fear cannot argue with: something to do. A watch order, a count of doors, a job.
By the second landing the spears are carried, not braced. Some of the young ones walk closer to Kaelen than to you. Trust, once it starts, is greedy.

ch25_breach.notes: GDD Ch25: the inner corridors are not empty - a Hollowed attack-wave panics the coalition soldiers. Held, and Kaelen is brought safely past. Drop is act4_crown_cinder.
text: The corridors are not empty. The Hollowed come out of the walls' old wounds in a disciplined tide - disciplined, which is the frightening part - and the young soldiers' spears shake.
You take the tide's head in front of them so the shaking has somewhere else to go. Courage is contagious, and so is the other thing.

ch25_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: the coalition's rearguard breaks the tide after you fall. Converges on ch25_descent.
text: You wake at the stair-foot with Veyra's cloak over you and the sound of a tide breaking apart somewhere behind.
The rearguard finished it. The young soldiers helped - and soldiers who have held a line together ask fewer questions about the man walking point.

ch25_descent.notes: GDD Ch25 close: the descent continues; the door to the throne room. Bridge to Ch26.
text: The last stair ends at a door grown out of the living rock - grey, veined silver, breathing faintly as the mist breathes.
Kaelen puts his palm on it. "She has been waiting three hundred years to be found interesting," he says. "Be polite about it. Do not give her the ending she is expecting."

ch26_open.notes: GDD Ch26 open: Ilsevet's shadow throne room in the deepest heart of Ashenmere.
text: The throne room is a hollow sphere of stone with the Blood Moon's light rising through a crack in the ceiling, and Ilsevet sits at the bottom of it like a woman at the bottom of a well, looking up.
Everything here is grey and silver, including her smile.

ch26_truth.notes: GDD Ch26: Ilsevet lays everything bare - she secretly accelerated the original Sundering, exploiting Kaelen's desperation as a tool.
text: She lays it bare like a butcher. The whisper at Saltmere: hers. The seven candles Kaelen prayed over: hers, rearranged. His desperation was her instrument, tuned for one use.
"Tonight I become one with the Hollowing completely," she says. "Not a curse. Perfection." Kaelen closes his eyes: three centuries of guilt, re-priced.

ch26_shockwave.notes: GDD Ch26: Ilsevet's preliminary corruption shockwave - the whole team shields Kaelen through it, exhausted but standing. Winning is the line holding. Drop is act4_tide_ash.
text: Her preliminaries arrive like weather: a tide of grey that fills the sphere floor to ceiling with a sound like a mountain learning to scream.
The team locks shields over Kaelen - Concordat iron, ranger bows, ward-light, you at the hinge of it. Hold, and the ritual begins. Hold.

ch26_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: Kaelen's own wards take the remainder of the shockwave after the line falls. Converges on ch27_open.
text: You wake face-down with the tide's taste in your mouth and Kaelen's voice still counting the ward-lines above you - hoarse, stubborn, unbroken.
His own wards took the last of it. Three centuries of holding doors, and he is still the best wall in Kaldareth.

ch27_open.notes: GDD Ch27 open: full-scale battle in the ruins at peak Blood Moon while Kaelen begins casting the Purification Ritual.
text: The sphere fills with the war it took three acts to build: shield-wall locking into ward-lattice, ranger lanes cutting the grey, the whole machine turning at once.
Kaelen begins to cast. The ritual takes him out of the fight the moment it starts - the moment Ilsevet stops being weather and becomes an arrow.

ch27_fight.notes: GDD Ch27: Ilsevet breaks through toward the vulnerable, channeling Kaelen. The DETERMINED outcome: the outer line yields ground to concentrate protection on him - she is held off long enough. Drop is none.
text: She comes through her own army like a rumor through a small town, and every yard you give her is a yard she spends not reaching the circle.
The DETERMINED order goes out: the outer line bends, deliberately, buying the centre everything it has. Yielding ground is not losing it - not tonight.

ch27_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: the coalition's three war-machines hold her off after you fall. Converges on ch27_begun.
text: You wake against the circle's outer chalk with the battle still standing where you left it, which is the only ending you asked of it.
The line held. All three of it - iron, bow, ward - without you, which is what an alliance is for.

ch27_begun.notes: GDD Ch27 outcome: the ritual begins - but its energy starts to fluctuate. Flag ch27_ritual_begun. Bridge to Ch28.
text: Ilsevet withdraws to the far side of the sphere, unhurried, cataloguing. The circle's light climbs - and stutters.
Oren reads the fluctuation and goes grey. "Her corruption is deeper in the Core than the working assumed. It needs more than the fragments. It needs an anchor that is alive and willing."

ch28_open.notes: GDD Ch28 open: the ritual's crisis - it needs a living anchor; Veyra steps forward without hesitation.
text: "A living anchor, willing," Oren says, and the sphere goes quiet enough to hear the Blood Moon rise.
Veyra steps forward before anyone can invent a reason she shouldn't. "I am here because I chose to be," she says. "Let me help finish this - together, not instead of you."

ch28_object.notes: GDD Ch28 alternate route: there is no other anchor; the outcome converges on the DETERMINED one.
text: You ask for another way, because someone has to. Oren gives you the inventory of none: the fragments are spent, the Core is occupied, and unwilling anchors corrupt the working.
Kaelen looks at Veyra. Veyra looks back, steady as a wall. Some choices are only ever going to end one direction; the asking was the point.

ch28_anchor.notes: GDD Ch28 Dilemma - DETERMINED: fully support Veyra's decision, protecting both her and Kaelen through the blood-anchor connection; the ritual stabilises. Flag ch28_anchor_set.
text: The connection takes blood and gives back light. Veyra holds Kaelen's hand inside the circle, and the fluctuation steadies like a room steadies when someone says the true thing out loud.
You hold the narrow ground between them and the dark. One blood bond, two names, one family three centuries in the assembling.

ch29_open.notes: GDD Ch29 open: Ilsevet merges herself with the Ritual Core so it can never be sealed; Kaelen calls out in genuine sorrow.
text: Ilsevet stops being a woman the way a river stops being rain. She pours herself into the crack in the Core, and the Core lets her - grey and gold, no ceremony, no retreat.
Kaelen calls out - not in anger. "You didn't have to become this to be strong, Ilsevet." Behind the monstrous geometry, an old human expression surfaces. Then it goes.

ch29_barrier.notes: GDD Ch29 Dilemma - DETERMINED: the whole coalition forms a final barrier around Kaelen and Veyra, holding Ilsevet back with everything left. Flag ch29_final_barrier.
text: The barrier is everyone: the shield-wall's last hour, the rangers' last arrows, the mages' last wards, Bryn's joint standard in the middle of it, and you at the seam.
She spends herself against it wave after wave, and the barrier spends back, and behind you the ritual counts toward its apex. One strike will decide everything.

ch29_guardfight.notes: GDD Ch29: one of Ilsevet's elite Vessels carves at the barrier's seam. Held, the barrier closes around Kaelen and Veyra. Drop is none - the reward here is the ritual surviving.
text: One of her elite Vessels carves at the barrier's seam - fluent, practised, aiming its grief at exactly the joint you are holding.
You meet it in the seam and close the joint behind you. The barrier mends. The ritual counts on.

ch29_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: Bryn's joint unit closes the seam after you fall. Converges on ch30_open.
text: You wake at the seam's edge with Bryn's standard planted over you and his joint unit closing the gap in disciplined silence.
The barrier mends without you, exactly as you taught them to mend it. That is the whole reward, and it is enough.

ch30_open.notes: GDD Ch30: the purifying energy touches Ilsevet and offers her freedom - the same offer given the whale at Saltmere and the tree at Sky Sanctum.
text: The ritual's apex is a held breath. Kaelen turns the purifying light on Ilsevet the way it was turned on a whale, once, and a tree: an offer, not a weapon. Freedom from the hatred that has eaten her for three hundred years.
The light waits. It has waited this long. She looks at it as the drowned look at the surface.

ch30_refusal.notes: GDD Ch30 Dilemma - DETERMINED: Ilsevet refuses the light; her avatar is undone by the purification wave - destroyed not by the team's violence but by her own choice. Winning is holding the channel open while the light does its work. Drop is act4_anchor_pearl.
text: "I have gone too far to go back," she says, and the refusal is the most human thing she has done all night. "At least let this mean something."
Her avatar rises for one last tide, and the purification wave comes down the channel you are holding open. Not your violence. Her choice, honoured at last.

ch30_lose.notes: Combat loss recovery: Kaelen and Veyra hold the channel from inside the circle after you fall. Converges on ch30_unmade.
text: You wake on the sphere floor with the light still pouring through where the avatar stood, patient as a tide going out.
The channel never closed. Kaelen and Veyra held it from inside the circle, which was always the plan the ritual preferred.

ch30_unmade.notes: GDD Ch30 outcome: the Hollowing is permanently sealed, the Mist Zones begin to fade, Kaelen survives - fully cleansed for the first time in three centuries. Flag ch30_hollowing_sealed. Bridge to Ch31.
text: The wave takes her apart as morning takes apart a nightmare: thoroughly, without malice, piece by refusing piece. The Core closes gold. The Blood Moon sets.
Kaelen - cracked glass going clear from the heart outward - stands and breathes like a man three centuries in arrears. The Hollowing is sealed. The mist is already thinning.

ch31_open.notes: GDD Ch31 open: a new dawn over Ashenmere's ruins; a world beginning to heal, three factions genuinely united.
text: Morning after the Blood Moon. The ruins of Ashenmere are gold-grey and quiet, and the mist beyond the walls is - visibly, measurably - thinner.
Kaelen smiles warmly for the first time in anyone's memory. Veyra holds his hand as family. Harwick, Ilyndra and Oren stand together, united by choice.

ch31_council.notes: GDD Ch31: Kaldareth is officially freed from the expanding Hollowing; Kaelen chooses to remain at Greyhold as advisor to the Vigil.
text: The council of three sits in Greyhold's old hall - the same neutral table, a different world. Kaldareth is declared free of the expanding Hollowing, in the flat voice of real documents.
Kaelen asks for one appointment: advisor to the Vigil. Close to the ward-records, he says. Close to family, says Veyra.

ch31_fields.notes: GDD Ch31 alternate route: the same outcome read from the ground - the land itself is the document.
text: You walk the walls at noon and watch the mist lose. Grass is coming up through the grey as it comes up through snow - in patches first, then as a matter of policy.
A farmer outside the gate asks if the fields will hold. You look at the sky, clean of everything for the first time in your adult life, and say: yes.

ch31_close.notes: GDD Ch31 outcome: Kaldareth freed, Kaelen remains at Greyhold as advisor. Flag ch31_new_dawn. Bridge to the Ch32 epilogue.
text: The Vigil takes the surrender of nobody. There is no army left to surrender; there is weather, healing. The Vigil watches anyway - that is what a Vigil is.
Kaelen remains at Greyhold, advisor and family. The war is over. The watching, gratefully, is not.

ch32_months.notes: GDD Ch32 epilogue part 1: the world heals - Emberfall, Harrow's Reach, Saltmere, all saved in Acts 1-2, pay off.
text: Months pass, and the map redraws itself politely: the Mist Zones shrink season by season, replaced by fields that behave like fields.
Emberfall holds its first clean harvest under Mother Senna and a grown-tall Elin. Harrow's Reach thrives under Reeve Callen, who dreams no more.

ch32_alliance.notes: GDD Ch32 epilogue part 2: Greyhold, Bryn's joint unit, Thessaly's redemption, Veyra and Kaelen, the brooch.
text: Greyhold loosens from fortress into a symbol of the alliance. Bryn commands a joint unit of all three peoples; Thessaly earns her redemption in careful research under Oren.
Veyra leads the Vigil with Kaelen beside her - advisor, and family. The brooch is kept as a reminder: old wounds heal, if someone is brave enough to try.

ch32_epilogue_gate.notes: CLASS GATE, epilogue. How the histories name the player depends on the class; three ways to be remembered.
text: And you - who first came to Greyhold as the sole survivor of a small village - are known across Kaldareth now, as part of something far greater.
The histories argue about what to call you. It depends, as it always did, on what you were.

ch32_epilogue_warrior.notes: Warrior epilogue: the bridge lesson, paid forward through Bryn's joint unit.
text: They name you the Shield of the Alliance. You drill the joint unit beside Bryn, and the lesson you teach is the one you learned on a bridge: break what blocks the road, and carry what cannot.
Harwick calls it the only doctrine worth a shield. He is not wrong.

choices.label: Stand in the peace you made

ch32_epilogue_archer.notes: Archer epilogue: the ford lesson, paid forward mapping the mist for Ilyndra's wardens.
text: They name you the Eye Beyond the Mist. You map the retreating grey for Ilyndra's wardens, and the lesson you teach is the one you learned at the ford: read the ground before it reads you.
The map has one colour less every season. You keep drawing it.

choices.label: Stand in the peace you made

ch32_epilogue_mage.notes: Mage epilogue: the rune-line lesson, paid forward rebuilding Arcanum around purification.
text: They name you the Litany Answered. You rebuild Arcanum's registry beside Oren around purification instead of fear, and the lesson you teach is the one you learned at the rune-line: read before striking.
Thessaly, granted her controlled research, reads every page. She never says thank you. She does not need to.

choices.label: Stand in the peace you made

ch32_kaldareth_healed.notes: THE ending of the game, per the GDD's Ch32 epilogue: Kaldareth at peace because it chose to heal together. reward_modifier scales the simulated payout; leaderboard_tag buckets the run.
text: Kaldareth is finally at peace - not because it was never broken, but because it chose to heal together.
From Emberfall's silence to a clean-rising moon: the survivor of a burned village stood at the centre of the healing of the world. The histories will argue about the rest.
